advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the standalone `is_file()` existence-only tests (test_recovery_module_exists, test_context_assembly_module_exists); the reachability/import tests already cover module presence via a real symbol-level contract.
evidence: The reachability tests (lines 65-86, 156-172) do `from rebar.llm.workflow import gate_dispatch` / `from rebar.llm.plan_review import orchestrator` and assert hasattr per symbol — importing the module already fails if the file is absent, so the standalone is_file() checks add only rename fragility.
advisory.finding: test_recovery_module_exists and test_context_assembly_module_exists are bare `is_file()` existence-only assertions with no structural contract beyond existence; they are change-detectors that break on a file rename and are fully subsumed by the reachability tests (test_moved_names_are_still_reachable_from_gate_dispatch / _from_orchestrator), which import the modules and would fail on absence with a real symbol-level contract.
scenarios: A future rename of plan_review_recovery.py or context_assembly.py breaks these existence tests even though behavior and the re-export contract are preserved.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove test_recovery_module_exists and test_context_assembly_module_exists; rely on the reachability tests whose module imports fail on absence.

coaching.coaching: Delete the change-detector / tautological test the existence-only module presence tests; do not re-pin it to the new source text — a test that only mirrors the implementation asserts nothing.
